policy: These amendments replace first-pass evidence only for named ranks where second-pass review found an honorific-number ambiguity, an incomplete correction, a still-awkward recommendation, or a remaining semantic-number mismatch.

amendments.reason: The first-pass target meant 'I think I have a fever' more directly than 'I seem to have a fever'.

confirmed_findings.observed: مجھے لگ رہا ہے کہ بخار ہے۔ / I seem to have a fever.
confirmed_findings.recommended: لگتا ہے کہ مجھے بخار ہے۔ / I seem to have a fever.
confirmed_findings.note: The impersonal لگتا ہے construction preserves the evidential/seeming nuance more closely.

amendments.reason: انہوں نے can be honorific singular; changing English to plural was overconfident. Use an unambiguously singular target for the singular English.

confirmed_findings.observed: انہیوں نے آج کیا کیا؟ / What did he do today?
confirmed_findings.recommended: اس نے آج کیا کیا؟ / What did he do today?

amendments.reason: انہوں نے may be honorific singular, so the first-pass plural-English change was not a safe correction for a standalone learner pair.

confirmed_findings.observed: انہوں نے میری پیشکش ٹھکرا دی۔ / He turned down my offer.
confirmed_findings.recommended: اس نے میری پیشکش ٹھکرا دی۔ / He turned down my offer.

amendments.reason: The first-pass plural-English correction ignored the honorific-singular reading of انہوں نے.

confirmed_findings.observed: انہوں نے مجھے اپنی زندگی کی کہانی سنائی۔ / He told me his life's story.
confirmed_findings.recommended: اس نے مجھے اپنی زندگی کی کہانی سنائی۔ / He told me his life story.

amendments.reason: The first-pass plural-English correction was not warranted because ان کو/وہ غلط تھے can encode respect; make singular person explicit in Urdu instead.

confirmed_findings.observed: میں نے ان کو بتایا کہ وہ غلط تھے۔ / I told him that he was wrong.
confirmed_findings.recommended: میں نے اسے بتایا کہ وہ غلط تھا۔ / I told him that he was wrong.

amendments.reason: The first-pass rewrite repaired agreement but collapsed English plural 'advances' into singular mass-noun 'progress' and rendered 'remarkable' loosely as 'splendid'. Preserve plural developments and the evaluative meaning explicitly.

confirmed_findings.observed: طب کے میدان میں حال ہی میں ہونے والے ترقی بہت شاندار ہیں۔ / The recent advances in medicine are remarkable.
confirmed_findings.recommended: طب کے میدان میں حالیہ ترقیات قابلِ ذکر ہیں۔ / The recent advances in medicine are remarkable.
confirmed_findings.note: ترقیات preserves the plural sense of advances; قابلِ ذکر aligns directly with remarkable; plural ہیں restores agreement.

amendments.reason: The first-pass plural-English correction ignored honorific ambiguity and also left الماری mismatched with English shelf.

confirmed_findings.observed: انہوں نے کتاب کو الماری میں رکھ دیا۔ / He put the book on the shelf.
confirmed_findings.recommended: اس نے کتاب شیلف پر رکھ دی۔ / He put the book on the shelf.

amendments.reason: انہوں نے may be honorific singular; retain singular English by making the Urdu subject unambiguously singular while also fixing ڈھیر.

confirmed_findings.observed: انہوں نے مجھے ڈھیڑ ساری خوبصورت تصویریں دکھائیں۔ / He showed me a lot of beautiful photos.
confirmed_findings.recommended: اس نے مجھے ڈھیر ساری خوبصورت تصویریں دکھائیں۔ / He showed me a lot of beautiful photos.

amendments.reason: The first-pass recommendation contained an awkward double سے construction.

confirmed_findings.observed: وہ پانچ دن کے لئے اسکول سے غیر حاصر تھی۔
confirmed_findings.recommended: وہ پانچ دن تک اسکول سے غیر حاضر تھی۔
confirmed_findings.note: Fixes غیر حاضر and uses پانچ دن تک for the duration.

amendments.reason: The first-pass plural-English correction ignored honorific-singular ambiguity.

confirmed_findings.observed: انہوں نے اپنی بیٹی کو پھل اور سبزیاں بھیجی۔ / He sent fruit and vegetables to his daughter.
confirmed_findings.recommended: اس نے اپنی بیٹی کو پھل اور سبزیاں بھیجیں۔ / He sent fruit and vegetables to his daughter.

amendments.reason: The first-pass مدد دی wording is less idiomatic than مدد کی in this construction.

confirmed_findings.observed: اس نے بزرگ کی سڑک پاڑ کرنے میں مدد کی۔
confirmed_findings.recommended: اس نے بزرگ کو سڑک پار کرنے میں مدد کی۔

amendments.reason: The first-pass version retained honorific-number ambiguity and used less natural مدد دی.

confirmed_findings.observed: انہوں نے بزرگ کی سڑک پاڑ کرنے میں مدد کی۔ / She helped the old man cross the road.
confirmed_findings.recommended: اس نے بزرگ کو سڑک پار کرنے میں مدد کی۔ / She helped the old man cross the road.
confirmed_findings.note: Urdu third-person singular is gender-neutral in this form, so singular English 'she' remains context-compatible.
